title: ADHD and biology — the overview
description: ADHD is supported by converging genetic, developmental, brain and treatment evidence. There is no single cause and no diagnostic brain or gene test — but the core machinery is well understood.

title: Brain development and structure
description: On average, the brain in ADHD matures on a later timetable, especially in prefrontal regions, with small differences in some deeper structures — largest in childhood.

title: The dopamine and noradrenaline supply chain
description: Six steps — make, store, release, clear, break down, self-tune. Simple parts; the complexity is in regulation, timing and how the steps interact.

title: Genetics — many small influences
description: ADHD is highly heritable, but through thousands of common variants of tiny effect plus rarer variants in some families. Genes describe risk in populations, not a diagnosis in a person.

title: No single dopamine story
description: Different studies point to different parts of the system, and some findings depend on medication history. ADHD is better described as several routes to a similar set of difficulties.

title: Explore evidence
description: Genes, brain development, the dopamine and noradrenaline machinery, treatment trials — and the open questions still being argued.

title: Open research questions
description: Five live questions arising from one person's observations — each with competing explanations and the observations that would tell them apart. Questions, not conclusions, and never a reason to self-experiment.

title: What treatment trials show
description: Randomised trials show the medicines reduce core symptoms in adults; a withdrawal trial shows frequent symptom relapse in previously stable adult lisdexamfetamine responders after switching to placebo. Registries suggest wider outcomes may improve, with important caveats.

title: MJB ADHD Guidebook
description: Start where you are. Each route ends in something usable.

title: Coordination and balance: understanding ataxia
description: Ataxia describes impaired coordination. A description of imbalance is a starting point for assessment, not proof of one inherited or degenerative condition.

title: Dopamine-responsive dystonia: a distinct clinical question
description: Dopa-responsive dystonia is a specific group of movement disorders. Improvement with an ADHD medicine is not equivalent to the clinical levodopa response used in its assessment.

title: Dystonia: patterned twisting and spasms
description: Dystonia is a movement disorder involving involuntary muscle contractions. This page helps you describe a pattern for assessment; a twisting sensation alone does not establish the diagnosis.

title: A field guide to the nervous system
description: Start with the affected function, the clinical pattern and the decision you need. Follow the evidence beyond slogans about a single chemical.

title: FND: diagnosis, active treatment and accountable care
description: Real symptoms deserve a positive diagnosis, symptom-specific rehabilitation, accessible support and a reviewed plan. Understand the options and what the treatment trials actually show.

title: Hereditary spastic paraplegia: what assessment looks for
description: HSP is a group of genetic conditions. This page explains why clinicians consider it and why a symptom resemblance or isolated genetic result is insufficient.

title: Parkinson’s: symptoms, treatment, genetics and care
description: A practical guide to recognition, motor and non-motor symptoms, treatment choices, medication continuity, genetics and research, with sources and questions to take to a specialist.

title: Prepare for an appointment
description: A one-page sheet that turns weeks of experience into the decision you need, three examples, and focused questions.

title: When treatment stops
description: A gap in a treatment that was working can quickly undo its benefit. Here is what the evidence does and does not show, and how to plan for continuity.

title: Dopamine-related treatments: different jobs
description: Precursor supply, reuptake inhibition, transmitter release and receptor activation are different interventions. Compare the indication and evidence as well as the mechanism.

title: When medication feels weak, inconsistent or inert
description: Check the exact product, delivery, timing and function before drawing a conclusion. A repeated difference deserves review; its cause is a separate question.

title: How ADHD medicines act
description: ADHD medicines influence catecholamine signalling through different transporters and receptors. Their mechanisms, timing and clinical evidence need separate comparison.

title: Understand treatment
description: What ADHD medicines do, what the evidence shows about benefit and harm, and what happens when treatment stops or restarts.

title: Restarting after a gap
description: Re-titrating cautiously is usually reasonable. Changing to a medicine that has already been tried and found inadequate is a different decision, and needs reasons.

title: Saffron and Mucuna: what the evidence actually says
description: Take botanical treatments seriously enough to examine the trials, the product and the unanswered comparisons. Promising does not mean interchangeable.

title: Fatigue, sleepiness and sleep disruption
description: Being sleepy, running out of energy and finding it difficult to start a task are different experiences. A useful appointment describes which occurs, when and with what other symptoms.

title: Understand your experience
description: Start from the difficulty you notice and turn it into observations a clinician can use.

title: Memory, time and awareness
description: Forgetting what you meant to do, losing track of time and acting on autopilot are different problems with different clues.

title: Burning, electric and touch-sensitive pain
description: Pain quality helps describe the problem, but does not diagnose nerve damage. This page helps you connect sensations with their distribution, associated findings and assessment.

title: Pain, fatigue and movement
description: How to describe physical symptoms clearly without assuming ADHD explains everything — or nothing.

title: Strong sensation, unclear position feedback
description: Pain, pressure, knowing where a limb is and coordinating an action are different descriptions. Record them separately so that an appointment can address each difficulty.

title: Stiffness, spasms and spasticity
description: Stiffness describes an experience. Spasticity describes a neurological examination finding. Bring the pattern and functional effects to assessment instead of having to choose the label first.

title: MJB ADHD
description: MJB ADHD separates established evidence, lived experience, policy critique and hypotheses about ADHD. General information and advocacy, not medical advice.

title: Genetics and ADHD: start here
description: ADHD runs in families. Twin studies put heritability at about 74% (Tier B).

title: The dopamine pathway, step by step
description: An explorable map of how a brain dopamine cell makes, stores, releases and clears dopamine, with sources and limits for every step.

title: Whole system overview
description: How do biology and context connect to cognitive function? This is an organising model, not one ADHD formula or a diagnostic graph.

title: Genes regulation and development
description: A genetic association and a molecular mechanism answer different questions. A pathway gene is not automatically an ADHD risk gene.

title: Amino acid supply and brain entry
description: Supply, transport and synthesis are separate control points. A blood level or dietary increase does not directly measure a synapse.

title: Catecholamine synthesis and cell type branches
description: The catecholamine branch depends on which enzymes a cell expresses. Not every dopamine-producing neuron makes noradrenaline or adrenaline.

title: Vesicle loading and storage
description: ATP powers the vesicle's proton pump. VMAT2 uses the resulting proton gradient to load monoamines for storage and later release; it is not directly powered by ATP. This normal mechanism does not establish an individual transport defect.

title: Release and vesicle recycling
description: Electrical activity, calcium entry and vesicle fusion are distinct steps. Vesicle membrane recycling is different from amino-acid recycling.

title: Synaptic clearance and intracellular metabolism
description: Transport out of the cleft and intracellular breakdown are different routes. MAO is not an enzyme floating freely in the synaptic cleft.

title: Receptors and intracellular response
description: Receptor coupling is a starting point, not a complete prediction. A receptor family cannot be labelled universally good or bad for attention.

title: Energy supply and neuronal demand
description: Neurons use energy to maintain gradients and support signalling. This is normal physiology, not proof of an energy defect in ADHD.

title: Dopamine and noradrenaline projection systems
description: Selected projection examples: schematic routes, not anatomical positions. Projection systems are not one-to-one maps from a transmitter to a symptom.

title: Large scale brain networks
description: Connectivity measures describe relationships in recorded brain activity. Dashed lines show statistical dependence, not axons or proven causal influence.

title: Cognitive functions and observable outcomes
description: A cognitive profile includes several functions and several kinds of measurement. No single transmitter amount predicts the entire cognitive profile.

title: BH4 synthesis and cofactor recycling
description: Making BH4, recycling it after hydroxylases and redox salvage are distinct. The hydroxylase cofactor cycle is not identical to NOS redox salvage.

title: Vitamin and mineral support
description: A required cofactor is not evidence that extra intake will help. Cofactor requirement does not establish deficiency or a supplement benefit.

title: Glutamate transmission
description: Glutamate transmission combines vesicle loading, receptors and uptake. An excitatory transmitter pathway is not a measure of ADHD severity.

title: GABA transmission and inhibition
description: GABA responses depend on receptor type and the ion gradient. GABA is usually inhibitory in mature contexts; that is not an absolute rule.

title: Serotonin supply and transmission
description: Brain and peripheral serotonin are separate compartments. Serotonin is not simply a happiness chemical; tissue context matters.

title: Acetylcholine and attention modulation
description: Acetylcholine is made, released, hydrolysed and its choline reused. DAT and MAO are not the main acetylcholine clearance pathway.

title: Astrocytes and transmitter recycling
description: Astrocytes support transmitter handling and the cellular environment. Amino-acid recycling is different from recycling a vesicle membrane.

title: Redox balance and glutathione
description: Glutathione participates in redox chemistry; balance matters. This normal redox system does not establish oxidative stress as an ADHD cause.

title: One carbon metabolism and methyl donors
description: One-carbon transfer and SAM-dependent methylation are linked processes. A biochemical pathway is not a personalised supplement prescription.

title: Sleep circadian timing and arousal
description: Circadian timing, sleep pressure and arousal interact but are not identical. Sleep loss can worsen performance without establishing the origin of ADHD.

title: Adrenal hormones: two tissue compartments
description: Cortisol and adrenaline come from different adrenal tissues. Peripheral stress hormones cannot be read as a brain dopamine measurement.

title: Development synapse formation and maintenance
description: Developmental biology and genetic association require different evidence. Rare-gene examples belong to the rare-variant source, not the 2023 GWAS.

title: Medication absorption metabolism and elimination
description: Drug exposure is not the same thing as synaptic transmitter metabolism. These steps do not supply a dose or justify changing a prescribed regimen.

title: Medication target overlays
description: Three medicines, different target actions: a simplified comparison. A target diagram is not a medicine ranking or a personal treatment choice.

title: Mitochondrial quality control: one mitophagy route
description: One mitochondrial quality-control pathway: PINK1–PRKN mitophagy. A normal quality-control pathway does not establish an ADHD mechanism.

title: Immune signalling and neural context
description: Immune signalling and neural context are research questions, not a universal cause. Established immune biology is not proof that ADHD is universally inflammatory.

title: Nutrition: supply, transport and evidence limits
description: Nutrients pass through absorption and regulated transport before brain use. Gut transmitter production is not a direct measure of brain synaptic supply.

title: Blood flow oxygen and glucose delivery
description: Oxygen and glucose have different delivery and membrane-entry routes. Reduced delivery and impaired cellular use are different hypotheses.

title: Histamine and orexin arousal modules
description: Histamine and orexin are distinct systems with interacting arousal roles. Neither system supplies a one-to-one map to an ADHD symptom.

title: Contextual genetic overlay
description: Interpret a genetic result through evidence, not a gene-name shortcut. Rare biochemical disorders and common ADHD association are not interchangeable.

title: TH reaction and regulation
description: Tyrosine hydroxylase chemistry: the reaction and its controls are separate. This is a cytosolic reaction; the arrow is not a direct route to a symptom.

title: DBH and PNMT compartment detail
description: DBH acts in secretory vesicles; PNMT acts in cytosol of expressing cells. These branches require the relevant enzymes; not every neuron has both.

title: DAT uptake and ion gradients
description: DAT transport uses ion gradients; ATP maintains those gradients indirectly. DAT is not directly powered by ATP hydrolysis.

title: PFC receptor signalling in a defined context
description: A specific experimental context: prefrontal working-memory circuits. More stimulation does not mean more benefit in every context.

title: Mitochondrial membrane and respiratory chain
description: Electrons pass along the respiratory chain while complexes I, III and IV pump protons. Proton return through ATP synthase supports ATP formation. This illustrates general cell physiology; it does not establish an energy defect in a reader.

title: BH4 hydroxylase recycling and salvage
description: Hydroxylase recycling and oxidised-BH2 salvage require different enzymes. Quinonoid BH2 and 7,8-BH2 must not be treated as one identical intermediate.

title: Glutamate glutamine cellular shuttle
description: The glutamate–glutamine shuttle links neurons and astrocytes. Astrocytic amino-acid recycling is not synaptic-vesicle membrane recycling.

title: Common locus to effector gene evidence
description: A genetic association identifies a region of interest. Connecting it to a candidate variant, gene and tissue-specific process requires several kinds of evidence. Each step has uncertainty; proximity alone does not establish causality.

title: Amphetamine dexamfetamine at the dopamine terminal
description: Amphetamine mechanisms: experimental targets and clinical effects are distinct. A therapeutic dose or individual benefit cannot be read from this cartoon.

title: What is ADHD?
description: ADHD as a recognised neurodevelopmental condition: persistent patterns of inattention and/or hyperactivity-impulsivity with real functional impact.
